6519.en: Let (R) be the radical circle of the Lucas circles, and let (L) = inverse in (R) of the circumcircle. Then (L) tangent to each of the 3 Lucas circles. Let A′ be the touchpoint of (L) and the A-Lucas circle, and define B′ and C′ cyclically. Then
re: X_6519 = radical center of the Lucas(12/11) circles
no: Let A'_{B} = inverse-in-A-Lucas-circle of B′, and define B'_{C} and C'_{A} cyclically. Let A'_{C} = inverse-in-A-Lucas-circle of C′, and define B'_{A} and C'_{B} cyclically. The six points A'_{B}, B'_{C}, C'_{A}, A'_{C}, B'_{A}, C'_{B} lie on a circle with center X_6519. The circle is here called the Moses-Lucas Circle. It and the circle constructed from 6 points at X_6449 are members of the Schoute coaxal system; the Schoute circle with center \(a^{2}(pS_{A} + qS)\) : \(b^{2}(pS_{B} + qS)\) : \(c^{2}(pS_{C} + qS)\) = pS*X_3 + \(qS_{\omega }\) *X_6
has radius R(\(S(p^{2}\) - \(3q^{2})\) ^1/2) / (pS + \(qS_{\omega })\). See X_6449 and X_6522. (Peter Moses, February 11, 2015)

A combo for X_6519 is found as follows: Let L_{A} and \(R_{A}\) be the center and radius of the A-Lucas circle, and define L_{B} and L_{C}, and also \(R_{B}\) and \(R_{C}\), cyclically. Let L* be the center of the Lucas inner circle and R* its radius. Then X_6519 = L_{A}/\(R_{A}\) + L_{B}/\(R_{B}\) + L_{C}/\(R_{C}\) + L*/R* + X_3/R. (Circle (L) is the Lucas inner circle, and A′B′C′ is the Lucas inner triangle.) (Randy Hutson, February 12, 2015)

re: X_6522 = radical center of the Lucas(-12/11) circles

The six points A'_{B}, B'_{C}, C'_{A}, A'_{C}, B'_{A}, C'_{B} lie on a circle with center X_6522. The circle is here called the Moses-Lucas(-1) Circle. It is a member of the Schoute coaxal system; see X_6519. Note that (L) is the Lucas(-1) inner circle and A′B′C′ is the Lucas(-1) inner triangle. (Randy Hutson, February 12, 2015)

Let Γ be the circumcircle and O(A) the A-Lucas(-1) circle. Let K_{A} = 1 if O(A) is internally tangent to Γ, and let K_{A} = -1 if O(A) is externally tangent to Γ. Define K_{B} and K_{C} cyclically. Let L_{A} and \(R_{A}\) be the center and radius of O(A), and define L_{B} and L_{C}, and also \(R_{B}\) and \(R_{C}\), cyclically. Let L* be the center of the Lucas(-1) inner circle and R* its radius. Then X_6522 = (K_{A}/\(R_{A})\) * L_{A} + (K_{B}/\(R_{B})\) * L_{B} + (K_{C}/\(R_{C})\) * L_{C} + L*/R* + X_3/R. (Randy Hutson, February 12, 2015)

6583.en: In the plane of ABC, let P be a point, and let A′B′C′ be the pedal triangle of P. Let A_{B} be the reflection of A in B′, and define B_{C} and C_{A} cyclically. Let A_{C} be the reflection of A in C′, and define B_{A} and C_{B} cyclically. Let N_{A} be the nine-point center of :g:`AA_{B}A_{C} << A A_B A_C >>`, and define N_{B} and N_{C} cyclically. The nine-point center of :g:`N_{A}N_{B}N_{C} << N_A N_B N_C >>` is here named the Hatzipolakis-Lozada Nine-Point Image of P. See `Hyacinthos 23083 <http://www.hyacinthos.epizy.com/message.php?msg=23083>`__. (Antreas Hatzipolakis and César Lozada, February 2, 2015)

6584.en: Let I = X_1, and let N_{A} be the nine-point center of IBC. Define N_{B} and N_{C} cyclically. Let K_{A} = X_54-of-IBC; i.e,, the Kosnita point of IBC, and define K_{B} and K_{C} cyclically. The circumcircles of the four triangles ABC, :g:`AK_{B}K_{C} << A K_B K_C >>`, :g:`BK_{C}K_{A} << B K_C K_A >>`, :g:`AC_{A}K_{B} << A C_A K_B >>` concur in X_6584; their radical center is X_484. Also, K_{A} = IBC-isogonal conjugate of N_{A}, and the points K_{A}, K_{B}, K_{C} lie on the line X_1X_3. See `Hyacinthos 23086 <http://www.hyacinthos.epizy.com/message.php?msg=23086>`__. (Antreas Hatzipolakis and César Lozada, February 1, 2015)

6585.en: The construction below for X_6585 is a tangential triangle variation of the construction described by Pavel Dolgirev: `Interest circle: open problem <http://www.artofproblemsolving.com/Forum/viewtopic.php?f=46&t=624821>`__. Let A′B′C′ be the Gergonne triangle of ABC; that is, the cevian triangle of X_7). Draw tangent lines from the vertices A,B,C to the incircle of A′B′C′ and let A_{1}, A_{2}, B_{1}, B_{2}, C_{1}, C_{2} be the points of intersection of these tangent lines with the sides of the triangle ABC. These 6 points lie on a circle, of which the center is X_6585. See `Hyacinthos 23112 <http://www.hyacinthos.epizy.com/message.php?msg=23112>`__. (Antreas Hatzipolakis and César Lozada, February 1, 2015)

6595.en: Let I = X_1, the incenter of a triangle ABC. Let L_{A} be the Euler line of triangle IBC, and define L_{B} and L_{C} cyclically. These lines concur in S = X_21, the Schiffler point of ABC. Let C_{2} be the point, other than S, of intersection of the line L_{B} and the circle (C, \|CS\|). Let B_{3} be the point, other than S, of intersection of the line L_{C} and the circle (B, \|BS\|). Let O_{1} be the circumcenter of \(SC_{2}\) B_{3}, and define O_{2} and O_{3} cyclically. The triangle :g:`O_{1}O_{2}O_{3} << O_1 O_2 O_3 >>` is here named the 1st Schiffler triangle. The triangles ABC and :g:`O_{1}O_{2}O_{3} << O_1 O_2 O_3 >>` are cyclologic, and X_6595 is the (ABC, :g:`O_{1}O_{2}O_{3} << O_1 O_2 O_3 >>`)-cyclologic center. See X_6596-X_6599 and `Hyacinthos 23098 <http://www.hyacinthos.epizy.com/message.php?msg=23098>`__ and `Hyacinthos 23101 <http://www.hyacinthos.epizy.com/message.php?msg=23101>`__. (S. Kirikami, A. Hatzipolakis and A.Montesdeoca, February 4-5, 2015)
